name: Rear Naked Choke from Invisible Collar
summary: The Rear Naked Choke encloses the neck from behind with the attacker's forearm and upper arm, supported by the other hand, while rear torso control limits the defender's movement.
description: Rear Naked Choke from Invisible Collar requires a separate back take. Establish rear torso control and the neck enclosure after leaving the facing high guard.
overview:
The attacker is behind the opponent with a secure torso connection and an arm able to pass around the neck. Invisible Collar is a facing guard clinch. Reaching the back is a separate positional change; the high legs do not themselves establish rear torso access.

Connect to the torso from behind before reaching across the neck. Control the defending hands without bending individual fingers or scraping the face. Arrange the forearm and upper arm beside the neck while preserving head alignment. Connect the arm loop with the support hand behind the head without levering the neck forward.

Never squeeze through the jaw or continue after a tap. Agree on verbal signals when the hands are occupied, and open the whole arm loop immediately.

Instructional sources: [Stephan Kesting — finishing the rear naked choke](https://www.grapplearts.com/how-to-finish-rear-naked-choke/); [Eddie Bravo — MTS 134 Invisible Collar in Austin](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KCyIwacRKu8).

flashcards.question: Rear naked choke practice: which arm routes form the harness before progressing toward the neck?
flashcards.answer: One under an armpit, the other over the opposite shoulder. The rear harness uses one underarm and one over-shoulder connection, with the hands joined. It retains torso attachment while hand fighting creates a later neck entry.

defender.name: from Invisible Collar Defender
defender.description: Rear Naked Choke from Invisible Collar (defender): Keep the attacking wrist from crossing into a complete neck enclosure. Hand fight before the supporting hand joins the choke.
defender.overview:
The attacker is behind the opponent with a secure torso connection and an arm able to pass around the neck. Invisible Collar is a facing guard clinch. Reaching the back is a separate positional change; the high legs do not themselves establish rear torso access.

Keep the attacking wrist from crossing into a complete neck enclosure. Hand fight before the supporting hand joins the choke. Work on torso position only while maintaining protection against the choking arm.

Do not rely on chin tucking or a violent head turn against the completed loop. Stop before dizziness, visual changes or loss of normal awareness. Turn and recover facing position once the neck enclosure has opened.

Never squeeze through the jaw or continue after a tap. Agree on verbal signals when the hands are occupied, and open the whole arm loop immediately.

Only after the neck grip and rear attachment have opened should you turn toward the opponent. Recover a near elbow and knee together as you face them, then use a small hip escape behind that frame to rebuild guard; moving the hips first while the head is trapped is unsafe.

Use both hands early: Hand fight before the supporting hand joins the choke.
Manage rear attachment: Work on torso position only while maintaining protection against the choking arm.
Keep the neck aligned: Do not rely on chin tucking or a violent head turn against the completed loop.
Tap promptly: Stop before dizziness, visual changes or loss of normal awareness.
Escape after release: Turn and recover facing position once the neck enclosure has opened.
